simple.meaning: עַשְׁתָּרוֹת (ʻAshtârôwth) appears 12 times in the Hebrew Scriptures and is introduced as a son in the family line and in connection with kingship.
simple.biblicalBackground: The first appearances are in Deuteronomy, Joshua, Judges, 1 Samuel, 1 Chronicles, beginning at Deuteronomy 1:4. BibleIQ detects the main surrounding context as family line, kingship, Israel.
simple.inThisVerse: In this verse, the tapped English word is source-aligned to עַשְׁתָּרוֹת (H6252) in the Hebrew text.
simple.whyItMatters: People in Scripture are understood by their place in the story. BibleIQ follows עַשְׁתָּרוֹת through the actual verses so the reader sees the person in context instead of as an isolated dictionary entry.
simple.summary: עַשְׁתָּרוֹת (ʻAshtârôwth) / H6252 is tracked through Deuteronomy 1:4, Joshua 9:10, Joshua 12:4, Joshua 13:12. The entry is generated from source alignment, occurrence evidence, and the surrounding Scripture context.

timeline.evidenceText: after he had struck Sihon the king of the Amorites who lived in Heshbon, and Og the king of Bashan who lived in Ashtaroth, at Edrei.
and all that he did to the two kings of the Amorites who were beyond the Jordan, to Sihon king of Heshbon and to Og king of Bashan, who was at Ashtaroth.
and the border of Og king of Bashan, of the remnant of the Rephaim, who lived at Ashtaroth and at Edrei,
all the kingdom of Og in Bashan, who reigned in Ashtaroth and in Edrei (who was left of the remnant of the Rephaim); for Moses attacked these, and drove them out.

Half Gilead, Ashtaroth, and Edrei, the cities of the kingdom of Og in Bashan, were for the children of Machir the son of Manasseh, even for the half of the children of Machir according to their families.
They abandoned Yahweh, and served Baal and the Ashtaroth.

The children of Israel again did that which was evil in Yahweh’s sight, and served the Baals, the Ashtaroth, the gods of Syria, the gods of Sidon, the gods of Moab, the gods of the children of Ammon, and the gods of the Philistines. They abandoned Yahweh, and didn’t serve him.

Samuel spoke to all the house of Israel, saying, “If you are returning to Yahweh with all your heart, then put away the foreign gods and the Ashtaroth from among you, and direct your hearts to Yahweh, and serve him only; and he will deliver you out of the hand of the Philistines.”
Then the children of Israel removed the Baals and the Ashtaroth, and served Yahweh only.

They cried to Yahweh, and said, ‘We have sinned, because we have forsaken Yahweh, and have served the Baals and the Ashtaroth: but now deliver us out of the hand of our enemies, and we will serve you.’
They put his armor in the house of the Ashtaroth, and they fastened his body to the wall of Beth Shan.
but the fields of the city, and its villages, they gave to Caleb the son of Jephunneh.

definitions.short: Ashtaroth , the name of a Sidonian deity, and of a place East of the Jordan
definitions.full: H6252. Ashtarowth III. עַשְׁתָּרוֺת proper name, of a location Ασταρωθ , etc., east of Jordan (name from worship of different forms of `Aštart; in Egyptian ±astiratu , as east Jordan located WMM As.u.Eur.162, 313 ; compare Tel Amarna proper name, of a location Aštarti ); — in Bashan (near Edrei) Deut 1:4 ( רֹת -), Josh 12:4 ; 13:12 , 31 (all + אֶדְרֶ֫עִי ), 9:10 ; 1Chr 6:56 = בְּעֶשְׁתְּרָה (i.e. עַשְׁתָּרָה בֵּית ) Josh 21:27 ; also קַרְנַיִם עַשְׁתְּרֹת Gen 14:5 ( ᵐ5 Ασταρωθ Καρναιν , compare GFM JBL xvi(1897), 155 f. who explains name as Ashtereth of the two-peaked mountain ); compare further, קַרְנַיִם Amos 6:13 ; — site probably either Tel ±Aštara , 21 miles east of Sea of Galilee, or Muzeirib , 8 miles further south; possibly both occur in OT; compare especially Dr Ashtaroth in Hast DB Di Gen 14:5 ), Buhl Georg. 248 ff. GASm Ency. Bib. 335 f .
